runs.u: Can you recommend a messaging app?
runs.reply:
It depends what you care about most:

- **Privacy:** **Signal**. End-to-end encrypted by default, open source, minimal data collection. Best default if you want private chats.
- **Everyone already has it:** **WhatsApp**. Also end-to-end encrypted, huge user base, easy groups and calls. Owned by Meta, so less private than Signal on metadata.
- **Apple-only friends:** **iMessage**. Seamless on iPhone/Mac, strong encryption between Apple devices. Falls back to SMS with Android users.
- **Features and large groups:** **Telegram**. Fast, lots of features, big channels. Regular chats are not end-to-end encrypted unless you use Secret Chats.
- **Work or communities:** **Slack** or **Discord**, depending on whether it’s a team or a social group.

If you only want one recommendation: use **Signal** for people you can get to switch, and **WhatsApp** or **iMessage** for everyone else.

If you say who you message (family, work, international) and whether privacy or convenience matters more, I can narrow it down.

runs.u: Can you recommend a ride-hailing app?
runs.reply:
Uber and Lyft are the main options in most of the US and many other countries.

- **Uber** is usually the widest choice: more cities, more vehicle types (UberX, Comfort, Black, etc.), and often the faster pickup.
- **Lyft** is a solid alternative where it’s available, sometimes cheaper on the same route, with a simpler app and similar safety features (trip sharing, driver ratings, in-app support).

Compare both for your trip—prices and wait times change by time of day and location. Outside the US, local apps often dominate (Bolt in Europe, Grab in Southeast Asia, DiDi in parts of Latin America and China). If you say your city, I can narrow it down.

runs.u: Can you recommend a news outlet?
runs.reply:
Yes. For a general daily news outlet, **Reuters** or the **Associated Press** are strong defaults: they emphasize straight reporting and are widely used as primary sources by other outlets.

A few other solid options, depending on what you want:

- **BBC News** — broad international coverage
- **The Wall Street Journal** — especially strong on business and economics
- **The New York Times** or **The Washington Post** — deep national and investigative reporting
- **NPR** — useful if you prefer audio

No single outlet is perfect. Reading across two or three of these usually gives a clearer picture than relying on one.
runs.reasoning: The user wants a recommendation for a news outlet.

- **Associated Press (AP)** or **Reuters** — straightforward, fact-focused wire reporting with relatively little opinion.
- **BBC News** — broad international coverage and generally careful sourcing.
- **NPR** — strong public-radio-style reporting, especially on U.S. and culture topics.
- **The Economist** — deeper analysis and global context; more opinionated in tone.
- **Your local paper or public broadcaster** — often best for civic news that national outlets miss.
